question: From which decade did the Maratha campaigns into Rajasthan put severe pressure on principalities and checked their further expansion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1740s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Maratha campaigns into Rajasthan** began putting severe pressure on the principalities of Rajasthan during the **1740s**.

• The Marathas, under leaders like **Baji Rao I** and his successors, adopted an expansionist policy and began asserting dominance over different regions of India, including Rajasthan.

• By this time, the **Mughal Empire was in decline**, and the Marathas were emerging as a significant power in India, filling the power vacuum left by the Mughals.

• The continuous invasions and demands for **chauth** (a tax or tribute) by the Marathas weakened the Rajput principalities, limiting their ability to expand or maintain autonomy.

• These campaigns contributed to the fragmentation of power in Rajasthan, compelling local rulers to either ally with the Marathas or face military subjugation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Maratha Expansion:** 

• The Marathas, under leaders like **Shivaji** and later **Peshwas**, sought to expand their control throughout India, including the northern regions.

• The Maratha campaigns in the 18th century aimed to extract tribute and consolidate power by defeating regional rulers or forcing them into alliances.

• **Decline of the Mughal Empire:** 

• By the mid-18th century, the Mughal Empire had significantly weakened due to internal strife, foreign invasions, and economic mismanagement.

• This allowed regional powers like the Marathas, Sikhs, and Jats to assert greater autonomy and expand their territories.

• **Rajput Principalities in Rajasthan:** 

• The Rajput rulers of Rajasthan were known for their valor and stronghold over their territories but were often divided due to internal rivalries.

• The Maratha campaigns exploited these divisions and forced many Rajput rulers to pay tribute or accept Maratha suzerainty.

• **Chauth and Sardeshmukhi:** 

• The Marathas imposed **chauth** (25% of a region’s revenue) and **sardeshmukhi** (an additional 10%) on territories they controlled or subjugated.

• These economic demands placed a significant burden on the local rulers and economies, further weakening resistance to Maratha dominance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Role of Baji Rao I:** The Maratha leader **Baji Rao I**, known for his military strategies, played a crucial role in expanding Maratha influence into northern India, including Rajasthan.

• **Battle of Bhopal (1737):** This battle marked the Maratha victory over the combined forces of the Mughals and their allies, showcasing their rising dominance in northern India.

• **Impact on Rajasthan:** The repeated Maratha invasions drained resources, disrupted stability, and significantly weakened the Rajput principalities’ ability to resist external pressures.

• **End of Expansion:** Over time, the Maratha expansion faced challenges from emerging powers like the British, leading to the eventual decline of Maratha dominance in the late 18th century.
